project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 217 (System exposes an observed accessor which returns a mapping of revealed node ids to observations)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 217 in a new policy-runtime plugin: the read side of the identical `question.*` interface an exploration policy is handed during replay. A policy-runtime `PolicyQuestion` fronts a campaign tree — the same `(node_id -> parent_id, depth, payload)` node model the frozen evaluator and the nightly canary already address — as the `question.*` object docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §11 names, and feature 217 is its `observed()` accessor: the revealed cells and their honest observations, as a mapping `{node_id: Observation}`. The tree owns the answer surface (it can name a node, give its depth and parent, and read the in-sample metrics a node's payload carries); the question owns only the reveal bookkeeping — the set of cells a policy has committed to look at — because a tree whose answers depended on how often it had been asked would not be a ground truth (the same world/question split feature 184 built for the bootstrap pool). The accessor is prefix-only by construction: it answers the observations of the revealed set and nothing else, so an unrevealed node is absent from the returned mapping rather than filtered out of it, and a policy cannot reach an unrevealed score, an absolute score target, a hardcoded node id, or the node's `is_null` status by any path (docs nullius-tech-architecture.md §10.2, §11; cq-8, cq-16; prd §4.2). The observation is derived from the node's own payload — the in-sample metrics and diagnostics the node carries — carried unchanged and attributed to the node id it was earned on, never rescored, never narrowed, and never carrying a field the barrier forbids. The plugin is a new workspace member (`packages/policy-runtime`, import name `policy_runtime`) discovered by the module loader's workspace scan, with its app-namespace seat at `src/app/modules/policy-runtime`; no central registry, router or app factory is edited.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (`src/app`) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in `src/app/modules/<member>/` are reached by namespace import (e.g. `app.modules.bootstrap`, `app.modules.artifacts`).
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under `tests/` is collected by `pytest` with `testpaths=tests`; each workspace member's own suite lives under `packages/<member>/tests/` and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly. Stdlib-only computation is the norm for a member that fronts already-computed values: the bootstrap member's fit is a dense Cholesky solve in `math.fsum` over a pure integer-hash stream, the canary replay is a plain sum over frozen bytes, so feature 217's member adds no third-party dependency. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition (a builder that raises would take composition down for every unrelated feature, so a builder returns `None` for a deployment that names no store rather than raising). A member never imports another workspace member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name — so the policy-runtime member owns its own `CampaignTree`/`CampaignTreeNode` value types (the same `(node_id -> parent_id, depth, payload)` node model the frozen evaluator and the nightly canary address) rather than importing canary's. Values are validated at construction and at the address seam; the observation is the node's honest payload-derived metrics unchanged (never a stand-in, never a field the information barrier forbids); a refusal names the node and the tree. Tests assert on observed behaviour with long narrative docstrings explaining the "why", and pin the adapter against the tree's own primitives so the wrapper and the tree cannot drift.

feature.description: System exposes PolicyObservation, the frozen payload a revealed node carries, derived from the node's own payload — the in-sample metrics and diagnostics the node's canonical JSON carries — attributed to the node id it was earned on, so `observed()` is a dict of `{node_id: PolicyObservation}` and the honest in-sample reading the tree exists to give is the only thing a reveal returns; it carries the node id and the payload-derived metrics, never `is_null` (readable by exactly one component, the replay scorer — prd §4.2, cq-8), never an absolute score target, never an unrevealed node's score, and never a hardcoded node id, because a policy that could read any of those would be reading past the prefix the information barrier promises it. PolicyObservation is a frozen value, validated at construction: the node id is a non-empty string and the metrics are the node's own, so a policy comparing two revealed cells reads each cell's honest in-sample reading and cannot move either.

System exposes CampaignTreeNode and CampaignTree, the policy-runtime's own frozen node and tree value types — `node_id` (a non-empty string, the one address a node is revealed on), `parent_id` (the parent node id, or `None` for a root), `depth` (a non-negative integer, zero at a root), and `payload` (the node's canonical JSON — the frozen bytes the replay reads back) — the same `(node_id -> parent_id, depth, payload)` node model the frozen evaluator and the nightly canary address, owned by this member rather than imported from canary because a member never imports another workspace member and reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name. CampaignTree is a set of nodes in a stable order: it sorts its nodes by `node_id` before anything is hashed or walked, refuses a node with an empty id, a negative depth, a non-canonical payload, a duplicate id, or a parent reference that is not a node in the tree, so a policy handed a tree can never be shown a dangling edge or a node it cannot address.

System exposes PolicyQuestion, the adapter that fronts one CampaignTree as the read side of the identical `question.*` interface docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §11 names, and feature 217 is its `observed()` accessor. The tree owns the answer surface — it can name a node, give its depth and parent, and read the in-sample metrics a node's payload carries — and deliberately carries no reveal history, because a tree whose answers depended on how often it had been asked would not be a ground truth; PolicyQuestion adds only the reveal bookkeeping, the set of cells a policy has committed to look at, the one fact a replay needs and a tree must not hold. `observed()` returns `{node_id: PolicyObservation}` for the revealed set only, ascending by node id — an explicit sort before the reduction, the ordering rule §12 states for a search frontier, so two reads of one question agree whatever order the reveals came in — and each observation is the tree's honest payload-derived reading of the cell, so the map is a pure function of the revealed set: the same cells revealed in any order return the same observations.

System exposes `observed()` as prefix-only by construction, so an unrevealed node is absent from the returned mapping rather than filtered out of it — the accessor iterates the question's own reveal set and builds one observation per revealed node, and a node the policy has not revealed is never a key of the mapping, never a value, and never reachable by introspection, attribute walking, or a stray `__dict__` access (docs §10.2, cq-16). The reveal set is the question's private state and the accessor reads it read-only, so a policy holding the mapping holds only what it has already seen, and the accessor answers no node outside that set however it is asked — which is the whole of "returns a mapping of revealed node ids to observations", and the property that makes the information barrier (no unrevealed scores, no `is_null`, no absolute score target) a fact about the accessor rather than a promise in a docstring.

System exposes `policy_question(tree)`, the one factory that turns a CampaignTree into the read-side `question.*` adapter a policy expects, so the identical-interface requirement is a single call site rather than a construction a caller could get wrong: the adapter is bound to the tree it fronts (its node addressing, its payload-derived observations are the tree's), it refuses a non-tree or a tree with no nodes at construction naming what was wrong, and two adapters of one tree answer identical observations and cell meta to the last field — the property that makes "one policy, both pools" a fact about the adapter rather than a promise in a docstring. The policy-runtime member registers a `policy-runtime` component under the application factory (`@register` in the package `__init__`, never a submodule), whose builder resolves the tree the deployment's artifact store holds — returning `None` for a deployment that names no store rather than raising, the degrade-don't-break stance every store-bound builder in this workspace takes — so a composed application carries the read-side question for the tree the process is actually pointed at, and its app-namespace seat at `src/app/modules/policy-runtime` exposes the composed component without making the `app` package depend on any workspace member at import time.

project_specification.integration_points: Fronts a campaign tree — the `(node_id -> parent_id, depth, payload)` node model the frozen evaluator and the nightly canary already address — as the read side of the `question.*` interface a policy is handed during replay. Registers a `policy-runtime` component the module loader discovers by workspace scan, beside the existing `bootstrap`, `artifacts`, `canary` and sibling components, without editing the app factory, middleware or settings. Adds the app-namespace seat `src/app/modules/policy-runtime` beside `src/app/modules/bootstrap`, `src/app/modules/artifacts` — a member seat per plugin, reached by namespace import. The observation it returns is the in-sample reading the replay scorer's `is_null`-aware scoring reads past: the barrier keeps `is_null` in exactly one component (the scorer), so `observed()` returns the node's payload-derived metrics and never the null flag.
project_specification.constraints: `observed()` must be prefix-only: an unrevealed node is absent from the returned mapping, never filtered into it, and never reachable by introspection, attribute walking, or a stray `__dict__` access (docs §10.2, cq-16). `observed()` must never expose `is_null` — readable by exactly one component, the replay scorer (prd §4.2, cq-8) — nor an absolute score target, nor a hardcoded node id, nor an unrevealed node's score. The policy-runtime member must not import another workspace member (e.g. canary); it owns its own `CampaignTree`/`CampaignTreeNode` value types and reaches shared shapes through `app.*`. `@register` must live only in the package `__init__`, never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process. The component builder must degrade to `None` for a deployment that names no store, never raise — the factory builds every registered component on every `create_app()` call. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention. All existing tests across the repository-level `tests/` tree and every sibling member suite must stay green.

implementation_steps.phase: Add the policy-runtime member `packages/policy-runtime` (import name `policy_runtime`) with its own `CampaignTreeNode`/`CampaignTree` frozen value types, the `PolicyObservation` payload, and the `PolicyQuestion` adapter. Implement `observed()` as the read side of the `question.*` interface — prefix-only, returning `{node_id: PolicyObservation}` for the revealed set, ascending by node id, never carrying `is_null` or an unrevealed reading. Add the `policy_question(tree)` factory and the `@register("policy-runtime")` component builder (in the package `__init__`), plus the app-namespace seat `src/app/modules/policy-runtime`. Write the member's own suite under `packages/policy-runtime/tests`, pinned against the tree's own primitives, and confirm the repository and sibling suites stay green.

project_specification.success_criteria: `observed()` returns `{node_id: PolicyObservation}` for the revealed set only, ascending by node id, and an unrevealed node is absent from the mapping rather than filtered into it. No observation carries `is_null`, an absolute score target, a hardcoded node id, or an unrevealed node's score; the information barrier holds. The policy-runtime member joins by workspace-scan convention with no edit to a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration, and does not import another workspace member. The member's own suite and every existing suite stay green.
